newsitem.title: SPAIN: Michelin slowing truck tyre production. [CORRECTED 11:00 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Michelin slowing truck tyre production. [CORRECTED 11:00 GMT]

text.p: French tyremaker Michelin has slowed production of truck tyres to meet market demand (corrects reference to demand) Europe, finance director Eric Bourdais de Charbonniere said.
"We're slowing down production today" but without introducing short-time working, he told reporters on a tour of Michelin's tyre testing facility in the southern Spanish town of Almeria.
He did not give estimates for the European truck market this year. (Corrects to delete erroneous reference to outlook for 1997.)
French car and truck manufacturer Renault SA said earlier this month when it released its 1996 truck sales that it expected a decline in the European truck market this year.

CS First Boston said in a report on the tyre business issued last month: "Heavy-duty truck manufacturers (in Europe) have noted that first-quarter 1997 orders are down over 15 percent and new order intake in even lower still. This is particularly important to Michelin, which is the leading truck tyre maker in Europe".
The U.S. truck market shrank last year and is expected to fall further this year but a decline from peak 1995 levels had long been anticipated.

Although truck tyres represent a small portion of Michelin's sales in volumes, French brokerage Jean-Pierre Pinatton estimated in a report issued in December that because of their higher prices, they represent roughly 40 percent of turnover.
Bourdais de Charbonniere said roughly half of truck tyres are sold to truck manufacturers and half in the aftermarket.
